historical_references.reference: Harion the Hermit, also known as Hariolus, was a sixth-century Christian hermit celebrated in the Eastern Orthodox Church. He was born in Syria and lived as a hermit in the desert. Harion is said to have lived for 140 years and was renowned for his miraculous abilities and asceticism. His relics are now kept in the Monastery of St. George in Amid (Diyarbakır) in southeastern Turkey.

Harion, also known as St. Hero, was a fourth-century Christian martyr in Spain. She was a virgin who was martyred during the Diocletian Persecution. Her story is that she was sentenced to be buried alive in a rocky tomb, but she was rescued by a dove who carried her out of the tomb and dropped her off at the doorstep of a Christian bishop. Harion is now venerated as a patron saint of martyrs, virgins, and women in labor.
